Which transcripts can the equivalence classes tell apart?

Source: R/identifiability.R
equivalence_identifiability.Rd

Salmon summarises the reads as equivalence classes: sets of transcripts with the number of fragments compatible with exactly that set. The abundance of a transcript is determined by these counts only when the classes separate it from the other transcripts. Two isoforms that always appear together in the same classes, for example, can exchange fragments without any change to the class counts.

equivalence_identifiability() reads the classes (salmon quant --dumpEq) and reports, for every transcript, whether it is identifiable from them: whether its abundance is fixed once the total of every class is fixed. This is a property of the classes observed in a sample, not of the posterior draws: a transcript can be non-identifiable and still show a small inferential variance (see Details).

Usage

equivalence_identifiability(
  paths,
  transcripts = NULL,
  ignore_after_bar = TRUE,
  max_dense = 400L,
  max_iterations = 50000L
)

Arguments

paths

Character vector of Salmon output directories (containing quant.sf) or paths to quant.sf files, or Oarfish output prefixes. Names, when present, are the sample IDs; otherwise the directory name (or the prefix) is used.

transcripts

Optional transcript IDs to keep in the result; the classes of all transcripts are used for the computation.

ignore_after_bar

Logical. Keep only the part of transcript names before the first | (GENCODE FASTA headers used as Salmon references).

max_dense

Largest block (number of transcripts) solved with a dense decomposition. Larger blocks use the iterative solver.

max_iterations

Maximum number of iterations of the iterative solver per block. The transcripts of a block that does not converge are not counted in that sample, with a message.

Value

A tibble with one row per transcript that has fragments and was resolved in at least one sample (transcripts of a block that did not converge in any sample are left out): transcript_id, n_samples (samples in which it has fragments and was resolved), n_identifiable (in how many of them it is identifiable), identifiable_fraction and identifiable (TRUE when identifiable in all of them).

Details

With M the class by transcript membership matrix of one sample, a transcript is identifiable when its unit vector lies in the row space of M, that is, when no vector of the null space of M changes its abundance. The function avoids the decomposition of the full matrix:

  1. A class with a single unresolved transcript resolves it (a class of one transcript does so directly); repeated until nothing changes.

  2. Transcripts that are members of exactly the same classes cannot be told apart: they are marked non-identifiable, replaced by their sum, and step 1 is repeated.

  3. What is left splits into independent blocks. Blocks of up to max_dense transcripts are solved with a singular value decomposition. Larger blocks need the Matrix package: two random vectors are projected on the null space with conjugate gradients, and a transcript with a non-zero coordinate is non-identifiable.

Limits:

  • Only class membership is used, not the conditional probabilities of --dumpEqWeights. Isoforms that share all their fragments have proportional weights, so they stay non-identifiable with the weights; other cases may be resolved by them.

  • The annotation is taken as complete, and the classes are those observed in the sample: a transcript can be identifiable in a deep sample and not in a shallow one. Transcripts without fragments in a sample are not assessed in it.

  • This is not the range of optima of Zheng et al. (2022), which needs their sufficient statistics and a linear program per transcript.

  • Human samples have one block of tens of thousands of transcripts linked by multi-mapping fragments; expect minutes per sample.

In the six GSE129540 samples of the uncertainty article, the estimates of non-identifiable transcripts differed more between two halves of the reads of a sample than those of identifiable transcripts of the same expression: a median absolute log2 ratio of 2.4 against 0.7 at 20 to 100 reads. The posterior draws call three quarters of both kinds uncertain, so the two measures are close to independent.

Oarfish output has no equivalence classes and gives an error.

References

Zheng H, Ma C, Kingsford C (2022). Deriving ranges of optimal estimated transcript expression due to nonidentifiability. Journal of Computational Biology 29:121-139. doi:10.1089/cmb.2021.0444

See also

equivalence_support() for the share of unique fragments, add_uncertainty() for the uncertainty measured by the posterior draws.

Examples

# Two transcripts that always share their classes, and one with its own
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "identifiability_example")
dir.create(file.path(dir, "aux_info"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines(
  c("3", "2", "tx1", "tx2", "tx3", "2\t0\t1\t10", "1\t2\t5"),
  file.path(dir, "aux_info", "eq_classes.txt")
)
equivalence_identifiability(c(sample1 = dir))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   transcript_id n_samples n_identifiable identifiable_fraction identifiable
#>   <chr>             <int>          <int>                 <dbl> <lgl>       
#> 1 tx1                   1              0                     0 FALSE       
#> 2 tx2                   1              0                     0 FALSE       
#> 3 tx3                   1              1                     1 TRUE
